headline: Medium risk: Authelia can feed Prefect workflow metadata through shared OAuth/HTTP surfaces, creating default-path leakage and cascading trust errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, while Prefect exposes an API surface for workflow metadata. No shared filesystem or direct parser bridge is documented, so prompt injection is not default-path. The plausible pathway is indirect content flowing through auth headers or metadata, making the blast radius limited and requiring unusual integration choices.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to ingest Authelia-derived headers or claims as free-form text
IF an operator copies Authelia output into Prefect task inputs without sanitization
mitigations: Restrict auth claims to fixed schemas
Strip untrusted text from headers before Prefect ingestion
Use allowlists for any copied metadata
Add a manual review step for auth-derived fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth flows; Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad egress. Even without explicit secrets fields, the pair can move identity or workflow metadata across services in default integrations. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards identity claims into Prefect task metadata
IF Prefect sends workflow metadata to external services over its default network path
mitigations: Minimize claims in OIDC tokens
Redact workflow metadata before export
Disable unnecessary outbound integrations
Separate auth logs from orchestration logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable resource scopes. The only documented overlap is network/API use, which creates coordination risk but not a strong write-write conflict. Because no stronger shared mutable surface is shown, severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or database
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to mutate the same workflow state without locking
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Add optimistic locking on shared resources
Scope each agent to read-only where possible
Document ownership of mutable endpoints

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and Prefect can consume workflow metadata, so a downstream orchestration step could treat auth-derived output as authoritative. There is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking, but the pairwise pathway exists in common integrations and can propagate a mistaken claim into workflow execution.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Authelia output as an unverified trigger for workflow branching
IF an operator wires auth claims directly into task parameters
mitigations: Insert a verification step before branching
Require typed fields instead of free text
Log provenance for every imported claim
Fail closed on malformed auth metadata

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia and Prefect are both open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU-only residency, or retention mismatches. Prefect does touch workflow metadata, but no conflicting compliance regime is documented for either agent. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise policy mismatch, but the evidence does not show one.
conditions: IF one deployment stores regulated workflow metadata in Prefect while Authelia logs identity data under a stricter policy
IF the operator imposes different retention rules on auth logs and orchestration logs
mitigations: Align retention settings across both systems
Avoid storing regulated data in workflow metadata
Review log destinations weekly
Document data-class handling for both services
